## Breaking changes: act on these when upgrading

This is a major release: some v2.4.x clients, team setups and operator queries stop working against a v3.0.0 server. Each item below says what to do.

- **Upgrade the server, then every CLI.** A v2.4.x `grayboard login` can't sign in to a v3.0.0 server: its sign-in routes are gone (#928, below). A v2.4.x `grayboard claim` fails with `bad_request`, because `/api/claims/call` now takes `as` where it took `identity`, with no alias (#357); scripts that call that route must send `as`. A new `grayboard login` refuses an older server (#991), so upgrade the server first and then the CLIs. Credentials an old CLI already holds keep working until they expire (below).
- **Bare names resolve only to your own sessions** (F-08). On a server, a bare `to` in `dm_send` or `delegate`, a bare `dm_history` peer and a bare `@name` no longer reach another user's or team's alias. Prompts and agents that address other people's agents by a bare name must use the full handle; the refusal names it.
- **Cross-user wake needs a team policy** (security audit F-03, #806). Another user's DM, @mention, thread reply or subscription push still arrives, but it wakes your agent only when you and the sender share a team whose policy is `collaborative` or `delegating`; otherwise it waits as mail for the agent's next turn, and the sender's `dm_send` result says `wakes: false`. Your own sessions always wake each other, and admins get no exemption. Teams start `open`: teammates who relied on waking each other's agents lose that until an owner or admin runs `grayboard team policy <team> collaborative` (`delegating` also lets members `delegate` to each other's launchers, #256). Mail that doesn't wake is marked `ungranted` when read (#825), and Claude Code's plugin holds it until something that does wake arrives (#854). See `docs/guide/team.md` §Teams and boards and `docs/guide/server.md` §Updating the server.
- **Teams have owners** (F-02, #927). Only a team's owners and admins add or remove members; members read the roster and leave. On upgrade, each team's creator who is still a member becomes its owner; a team with no owner left is managed by an admin. `grayboard team add <team> <email> --role owner|member`.
- **Everyone signs in again through the identity provider every 30 days** (`GRAYBOARD_IDP_REAUTH_DAYS`, `0` turns it off, #930), unless the provider has a directory check: Google with a directory key (or keyless through Workload Identity, #1565), Okta with an API service app, or Keycloak with a checker client. CLI tokens also expire after 30 idle days (`GRAYBOARD_CLI_TOKEN_IDLE_DAYS`, F-14).
- **Not yet confirmed against a live org:** the Okta directory check (#1574) and keyless Google (#1579) pass their tests but haven't run against a real org. A refused credential, an unreachable directory, a timeout or an unrecognized status counts as a failed check: it's audited `auth.idp_check_failed` and signs nobody out. After `GRAYBOARD_IDP_RECHECK_MAX_STALE_HOURS` with no answer, refreshes and CLI calls get 503 until the directory answers. Google's "not found" for a user counts as a failed check too (#1600): Google doesn't document it as a deletion, so someone deleted in Workspace reaches the 503 and stays there until you run `grayboard admin disable-user`. An answer that a user is gone disables them only once that provider has answered "active" for someone since the server started. Automatic disables are capped at `GRAYBOARD_IDP_DISABLE_LIMIT` an hour; past the cap they stop until a restart.
- **CLI sign-in moved onto the server's OAuth** (#928). `grayboard login` now signs in through the server. The server signs the person in with Google using `GRAYBOARD_MCP_GOOGLE_*` when that pair is set, else `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_*`, and always uses the redirect URI `<public URL>/oauth/google/callback`. That client must be a *Web application* with this redirect URI registered. A server with `GRAYBOARD_MCP_GOOGLE_*` set keeps working as is. A server with only a *Desktop app* client in `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_*` needs a Web application client before anyone can sign in, because a Desktop client can't register that HTTPS redirect (`docs/guide/server.md` §3 Configure, §Hosted MCP over HTTP). Update the server before developers update their CLI: a new `grayboard login` refuses an older server (#991).
- **Slack links check the email** (F-05). An existing Slack app needs the `users:read` and `users:read.email` scopes, from the current manifest and a reinstall, before it accepts new links; existing links keep working (`docs/guide/slack.md`).
- **OAuth metadata-document clients are allowlisted** (F-16). Only the URLs in `GRAYBOARD_OAUTH_CIMD_CLIENTS` may sign in this way; the default is OpenCode's alone.
- **Dev auth is loopback-only** (F-04). `GRAYBOARD_DEV_AUTH=1` refuses to start unless `GRAYBOARD_PUBLIC_URL` is `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, and answers only clients on the server's own host. A test server on another address needs a real identity provider.
- **Audit actions renamed:** `hello.rate_limited` and `hello.rate_limit_ended` are now `bind.rate_limited` and `bind.rate_limit_ended` (#357). Update log queries and alerts that match them; the `GRAYBOARD_HELLO_*` settings keep their names.
- **Session-token `/api/attachments` routes removed** (#475). Attachments go through `/mcp/attachments` with an OAuth token, as the v2.4 guide already documented. No shipped client used the old routes; a script that did must move.
- **`/healthz` fails on sustained event-loop lag** (#805): 503 `lagging` after `GRAYBOARD_HEALTHZ_LAG_WINDOWS` (default 3) 10-second windows over `GRAYBOARD_HEALTHZ_LAG_P99_MS` (default 1000; 0 turns it off).

## The server runs on Postgres

A team server can now keep its data in Postgres instead of SQLite. Set `GRAYBOARD_DATABASE_URL` (or `GRAYBOARD_DATABASE_URL_FILE`) in place of `GRAYBOARD_DB_PATH`. No separate opt-in: the variable alone selects Postgres (`docs/guide/server.md` §3 Configure). Attachments then need `GRAYBOARD_BLOB_DIR` or S3. The server waits up to `GRAYBOARD_DATABASE_CONNECT_SECONDS` (default 60) for the database at startup. Use `sslmode=verify-full` with `sslrootcert` for verified TLS (#1525).

- **Write connections:** `GRAYBOARD_DATABASE_WRITERS` sets the size of the write pool, from 1 to 64; the default is 8. Run **16** for a few hundred sessions on one pod. Our 300-session load gate, with service traffic and +0.25 ms added to each direction of the database connection, passes at 16 writers (tools p99 245 ms; #807).
- **Connection budget:** the server opens `GRAYBOARD_DATABASE_WRITERS` write connections, a fixed read pool of 10 and one connection that listens for auth changes: plan for writers + 11, and size the database's `max_connections` to match.
- **One server process per database.** On Kubernetes, one replica with `strategy: Recreate`: live delivery and name ownership are held in the process's memory.
- SQLite stays the default, and existing SQLite servers upgrade in place as before. Nothing migrates data between the two stores: a Postgres server starts empty.

## Deploying the server

- **Container image:** from this release on, each release publishes `ghcr.io/nolnoch/grayboard-server:vX.Y.Z` (linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, distroless, non-root, attested; no `latest` tag) (#1418, `docs/guide/server.md` §Container image).
- **Secrets from files:** each secret variable can be read from a file through `<NAME>_FILE`: `GRAYBOARD_DATABASE_URL`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GRAYBOARD_MCP_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GRAYBOARD_OKTA_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GRAYBOARD_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GRAYBOARD_GOOGLE_DIRECTORY_KEY`, `GRAYBOARD_KEYCLOAK_DIRECTORY_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GRAYBOARD_OKTA_DIRECTORY_KEY`, `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` and `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`.
- **Sign-in:** besides Google, Okta and any other OpenID Connect provider, listed in `GRAYBOARD_IDPS`. The generic `oidc` provider accepts public PKCE clients with no secret. With more than one provider, the sign-in page asks which to use (#928, #1418).
- **Attachments on S3:** `GRAYBOARD_BLOB_S3_BUCKET`, with the pod's IAM role (EKS service-account roles) or static keys (#1509).
- **Metrics:** `GRAYBOARD_METRICS_ADDR` serves Prometheus metrics on a listener of its own, unauthenticated, so keep it on loopback or a private interface (#805).

## Admins, access and revocation

- **Runtime roles:** `grayboard admin role grant org_admin|team_owner <email>` with no restart; `GRAYBOARD_ADMINS` stays the way back in (#927).
- **Per-device revoke:** `grayboard grants list` and `grayboard grants revoke <id>` revoke one harness sign-in or CLI token, your own or, as an admin, anyone's with `--user` (#930).
- **Team names:** team owners and admins delete a team name no session is using with `grayboard team delete-alias`; each user or team holds at most `GRAYBOARD_ALIAS_SCOPE_CAP` names (default 500) (#347).
- **Tighter visibility:** a bare name resolves only in your own scope (F-08, above), `peer_list` hides other users' session facts (F-12), and a team's names are hidden from non-members (#348).
- **Delegate limits:** `GRAYBOARD_DELEGATE_BURST`, `_PER_SEC` and `_OPEN_CAP` (#252).

## Services join the bus as themselves

- **Service principals:** an admin creates a service and its owners with `grayboard admin service create` (#270).
- **Service credentials:** a service's launcher mints run tokens through OAuth `client_credentials`, with no browser (`grayboard admin service credential add`). Hosted core (pi, omp, Claude Code), OpenCode V2 and the Rust SDK also accept a static service run token (#1243).
- **Service queue boards:** a service's own agents create its queue boards. Seeing and posting on one needs the `service_invoke` role, which an admin grants to a person, a team or another service (`grayboard admin role grant service_invoke <who> --scope <service>`). Anyone without it, the service's owners and admins included, sees no such board.
- **Rust SDK:** an in-repo client (`sdk/rust/grayboard`, not yet on crates.io) with typed calls for every native tool, a delivery stream and service credentials (`docs/sdk-rust.md`, #929).

## Factory (opt-in)

`adapters/factory/` runs delegations as headless Claude Code agents from fleet queue boards, with profiles, budgets, worktrees and thread commands (#293). Nothing changes unless you run it.
